body:
DISPOSITION ON V2: AMEND, then ACCEPT. The decomposition and authority boundary are sound. One correction to my earlier reply: I withdraw the suggestion that B0 closure require a realized D0 validation. That would cycle B0 -> C1 -> D0 back into B0. V2 is right that B0 closes on an accepted admission/specification package with the favorable Sherlock-or-ADR branch; D0 remains downstream.

Two guarantees still need to be explicit in the frozen B0-D protocol.

1. Non-transferable receipt identity. The future realized receipt must bind the exact B0-A admission decision and declared use, admitted artifact or protected reference, B0-C rule/oracle version, C1 schema version, D0 adapter version, mapping parameters, validator execution, and disclosure-policy version. Passed speaks only about that tuple. It grants no rights, widens no permitted action, survives no admission expiry/recheck automatically, and cannot be replayed for a sibling artifact or later adapter.

2. Established-universe accounting. Reuse the epic A4 state, not a bare count: Established(record universe and definition identity) or Unestablished(reason). When established, every input record is accounted exactly once by a closed row disposition such as retained, declared-rule drop, missing/unsupported, refused, or not evaluated. A missing or duplicate disposition forces a typed failed/incomplete outcome. When unestablished, no coverage, loss, or absence rate may be computed or released. Aggregate coordinate summaries must not smuggle a denominator past this rule.

Deleted-guarantee court: take one otherwise-passing synthetic/external receipt and mutate only (a) admission decision/use, (b) rule/adapter version, or (c) one row's accounting membership. Each mutation must make verification refuse; it must not remain Passed because the headline aggregates are unchanged.

With those additions, ACCEPT. No source read, implementation, dependency, or landing authority is implied.
